parks.name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
parks.story: Historic mountain pass and trail network on the Kentucky–Tennessee–Virginia border.

parks.name: Mammoth Cave National Park
parks.story: Large karst landscape centered on an extensive cave system, with surface trails, river recreation, and guided cave tours.

parks.name: Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge
parks.story: Public wildlife refuge protecting bottomland hardwoods and wetlands in western Kentucky.

parks.name: Ohio River Islands National Wildlife Refuge
parks.story: A chain of river islands and mainland tracts along the Ohio River supports trails and wildlife viewing. Most sites have few facilities, so visitors should plan for limited services.

parks.name: Big South Fork National Recreation Area
parks.story: Rugged Cumberland Plateau recreation area with river gorges, forests, hiking, horseback riding, and camping.

parks.name: Fort Donelson National Battlefield
parks.story: Civil War battlefield and national cemetery site spanning the Kentucky–Tennessee region. Visitors can explore historic landscapes and interpretive areas.

parks.name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historic Site
parks.story: Commemorates Abraham Lincoln’s birthplace with a memorial building, visitor center, and historic grounds.

parks.name: Carr Creek State Park
parks.story: Recreation park on Carr Creek Lake with a campground, utility hookups, beach, and playground.

parks.name: Columbus Belmont State Park
parks.story: Historic Civil War site above the Mississippi River with earthworks, a museum, trails, and a campground. The campground operates year-round, although some water services are seasonal.

parks.name: Dawkins Line Rail Trail State Park
parks.story: A 36-mile rail trail linking Hagerhill in Johnson County with Evanston in Breathitt County. It is open to hikers, cyclists, and horseback riders, with trailheads and trestles along the route.

parks.name: E.P. 'Tom' Sawyer State Park
parks.story: Urban recreation park in Louisville with sports courts, walking trails, an archery range, and a seasonal outdoor pool.

parks.name: Fishtrap Lake Wildlife Management Area
parks.story: A large public wildlife management area surrounding much of Fishtrap Lake, with forested ridges, hunting, fishing, boating, and wildlife viewing opportunities.

parks.name: Fort Boonesborough State Park
parks.story: A reconstructed frontier fort interprets Kentucky’s early settlement history beside the Kentucky River. The park also offers trails, boating access, and campground facilities when available.

parks.name: General Burnside State Park
parks.story: An island park on Lake Cumberland with a public golf course, boat launch, campground, and picnic areas.

parks.name: Grayson Lake State Park
parks.story: A lakeside recreation park in northeastern Kentucky with boating, fishing, and outdoor activities.

parks.name: Green River Lake State Park
parks.story: Lake-centered recreation park with camping, boating, fishing, and shoreline activities.

parks.name: John James Audubon State Park
parks.story: Park and nature preserve celebrating naturalist John James Audubon, with a museum, nature center, boardwalks, and hiking trails. Pets are restricted on most preserve trails.

parks.name: Kincaid Lake State Park
parks.story: A lakeside recreation park in northern Kentucky offering fishing, boating, and camping.

parks.name: Kingdom Come State Park
parks.story: Mountain park in eastern Kentucky with scenic overlooks and outdoor recreation.

parks.name: Lake Malone State Park
parks.story: Lakeside park with primitive tent sites, RV hookups, hiking trails, a swimming beach, and boat access.

parks.name: Levi Jackson Wilderness Road State Park
parks.story: A local park near London focused on the Wilderness Road and early settlement history, with outdoor recreation and heritage features.

parks.name: Lincoln Homestead State Park
parks.story: Historic park interpreting the Lincoln family’s early Kentucky connections, with historic homes, reconstructed buildings, a museum area, and picnic/playground facilities.

parks.name: Mineral Mounds State Park
parks.story: Lake Barkley-side recreation property with a golf course, picnic area, fishing pier, and boat ramp.

parks.name: My Old Kentucky Home State Park
parks.story: Historic Federal Hill mansion and gardens associated with Stephen Foster, with golf, picnicking, and seasonal events.

parks.name: Nolin Lake State Park
parks.story: Lake-area park with boat access, trails, and camping.

parks.name: Old Fort Harrod State Park
parks.story: Historic site centered on a full-scale replica of the 1774 fort, with a museum, pioneer-era buildings, monuments, and cemetery grounds.

parks.name: Paintsville Lake State Park
parks.story: Lake park in eastern Kentucky with full-service RV and walk-in sites, boating, fishing, kayak access, and lakeside recreation areas.

parks.name: Taylorsville Lake State Park
parks.story: Lake recreation park with boating, fishing, birding, hiking, and horseback riding. The multi-use trail network supports hikers, cyclists, and equestrians.

parks.name: Yatesville Lake State Park
parks.story: Mountain reservoir park with RV, primitive, boat-in, and hike-in campsites, boating, fishing, golf, and multi-use trails.

parks.name: Barren River Lake State Park
parks.story: Resort park on a large lake with camping, boating, fishing, golf, and family recreation. Major 2026 renovations affect lodging and dining services.

parks.name: Blue Licks Battlefield State Park
parks.story: Historic battlefield and resort park with trails, a pioneer museum, lodging, and a seasonal campground.

parks.name: Buckhorn Lake State Park
parks.story: Mountain resort park overlooking Buckhorn Lake with lodge rooms, cottages, dining, and hiking trails. Pool and beach facilities are seasonal.

parks.name: Carter Caves State Park
parks.story: Cave and forest park with guided cave tours, trails, a lodge, and several camping options.

parks.name: Cumberland Falls State Park
parks.story: Known for a 125-foot waterfall and the rare moonbow, this park offers hiking, camping, cabins, horseback riding, and river scenery.

parks.name: Dale Hollow State Park
parks.story: Lake resort park with lodge rooms, cabins, golf, boating, trails, and equestrian-friendly camping. Winter lodging is limited to selected nights.

parks.name: General Butler State Park
parks.story: Hillside resort park near the Ohio and Kentucky river confluence with lake trails, historic house, lodge, cottages, and year-round camping.

parks.name: Greenbo Lake State Park
parks.story: Lake resort park honoring writer Jesse Stuart, with lodging, RV and primitive camping, hiking, mountain biking, and horseback trails.

parks.name: Jenny Wiley State Park
parks.story: Mountain resort park near Prestonsburg with a lake, trails, lodge, cottages, and boat-in camping.

parks.name: Kenlake State Park
parks.story: Lake resort park on Kentucky Lake with lodge, cottages, marina, and water-based recreation.

parks.name: Kentucky Dam Village State Park
parks.story: Resort park on Kentucky Lake with lodging, golf, marina access, fishing, and family recreation.

parks.name: Lake Barkley State Park
parks.story: Lake resort park with camping, cottages, marina access, fishing, and outdoor recreation on Lake Barkley.

parks.name: Lake Cumberland State Park
parks.story: Large-lake resort park offering cabins, camping, boating, fishing, and trails. The campground operates year-round, but water facilities close seasonally and other amenities are under renovation.

parks.name: Natural Bridge State Park
parks.story: Forest park known for a large natural sandstone arch, hiking trails, lodge, cottages, and camping. Some trails and attractions can close for repairs or seasonally.

parks.name: Pennyrile Forest State Park
parks.story: Forest and lake resort park with lodge, cottages, camping, hiking, golf, and seasonal beach/pool facilities. Equestrian camping remains available year-round.

parks.name: Pine Mountain State Park
parks.story: Mountain resort park overlooking the Kentucky Ridge with lodging, cottages, trails, and golf.

parks.name: Rough River Dam State Park
parks.story: Lake resort park with lodge, cottages, marina, trails, and fishing. A small air-camp site provides overnight camping near the park airport.

parks.name: Big Bone Lick State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic site and nature preserve with fossil beds, trails, a museum, and campground facilities.

parks.name: Breaks Interstate State Park
parks.story: Interstate park straddling the Kentucky–Virginia border, known for the Breaks canyon, overlooks, trails, and outdoor recreation.

parks.name: Dr. Thomas Walker State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic site commemorating explorer Dr. Thomas Walker and his early expedition into Kentucky, with a reconstructed cabin and heritage interpretation.

parks.name: Jefferson Davis State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic site honoring Jefferson Davis, with a monument and interpretive grounds.

parks.name: Old Mulkey Meetinghouse State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic meetinghouse and cemetery site preserving an early Kentucky religious landmark. Visitor services and tours may operate seasonally.

parks.name: Perryville Battlefield State Historic Site
parks.story: Civil War battlefield preserving the landscape of the 1862 Battle of Perryville, with interpretive trails, historic grounds, and visitor exhibits.

parks.name: Waveland State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic plantation-era house and grounds in Lexington with guided interpretation and gardens.

parks.name: White Hall State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic White Hall estate and former home of Cassius Marcellus Clay, managed by Eastern Kentucky University.

parks.name: Wickliffe Mounds State Historic Site
parks.story: Archaeological and cultural site interpreting a prehistoric Mississippian settlement and regional Indigenous history, with museum exhibits and grounds.

parks.name: William Whitley House State Historic Site
parks.story: Historic house and grounds associated with Kentucky pioneer William Whitley.

parks.name: Fort Heiman National Battlefield
parks.story: Fort Heiman is a Civil War battlefield unit associated with Fort Donelson National Battlefield in western Kentucky.

parks.name: Trail of Tears National Historic Trail
parks.story: A multi-state historic trail commemorating the forced removal of Cherokee people. It is a route with many separate sites rather than one continuously gated park.

parks.name: Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area
parks.story: A large multi-use recreation area between Kentucky and Tennessee with forests, lakes, trails, wildlife viewing, and camping.
